### Observed differences

- Six activities became mandatory: A22, A31, A32, A37, A38 and A39 each ran in about 48–52 in 100 cases in the earlier window but in all 200 cases in the later window, exactly once per case in both windows (no repetitions in either). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]

- A22 and the five-activity group A31/A32/A37/A38/A39 changed from alternatives to sequential steps: in the earlier window A22 and each group member never shared a case (A22 alone in about 48 in 100 cases, the group alone in about 52 in 100), while in the later window they occur together in every case, with the group before A22 in all 200. A22 also now always follows A23 and A21 and precedes A26, where earlier A26 usually ran without A22. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL013, REL014, REL001, REL007]

- The group was repositioned earlier in the case and swapped order with A23 and A21: the group's mean event position moved from about 0.58–0.59 to about 0.39–0.40 of the case; A23 moved from before the group (before it in about 52 in 100 earlier cases, mean position about 0.38) to after it (group first in all later cases, mean position about 0.48); A21 likewise moved from before the group (mean position about 0.53) to after it (about 0.61). [POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS004, POS002, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL008, REL012]

- Routing around the group changed: in the later window A20's observed outgoing transitions are the five group activities (shares about 0.15–0.24 each) where earlier A20 led only to A23; A21 now leads only to A22 where earlier it led to A22 in about 48 in 100 cases and to a group activity otherwise; and each group activity now shows A23 among its observed successors (about 0.15–0.25) where it previously showed A26, while A26 still follows the group in every later case. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL025]

- The group's internal order stays unfixed in both windows, with both orders in similar proportions (e.g., A31 before A32 in about 25 vs 28 in 100 earlier cases and about 47 vs 53 in 100 later cases). [REL030, REL039]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process was restructured around the group A31, A32, A37, A38, A39: a branch that in the earlier window ran at most once, in about half of the cases, as an alternative to A22 and sat between A21 and A26 (after A23), in the later window runs exactly once in every case, directly after A20 and before A23, while A22 — itself now mandatory — always runs after the group. Accordingly, A20 now leads into the group instead of A23, the group flows on to A23 instead of A26, and A21 always leads to A22 instead of branching into the group. [OCC001, OCC002, REL015, REL020, REL008, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS005]

The support is direct and consistent: the order swaps and the alternatives-to-sequential change are shown relationally (co-occurrence of A22 with each group member rises from 0 to 100 in 100; A23–group and A21–group orders flip), the routing change is shown in the successor profiles, and participation, position and relation items all point the same way across all 62 qualifying items — far above the fewer than one item (0.67 of 134 units) expected by chance in a stable process. Limitations: the windows are finite samples, the group's internal sequence remains variable, and the evidence cannot rule out that the later window captures only a subpopulation of cases (for example cases that always execute the group) rather than a modified process. [REL015, REL020, REL008, DIR001, DIR007, POS009]

Other differences: A39 immediately follows A31 in about 52 in 100 later cases versus about 30 in 100 earlier cases (based on 53 and 90 observations), and A20's mean event position moved slightly earlier (about 0.35 to 0.31); both fit the same reordering rather than a separate change. [LAG001, POS001]
